title: Decode: low-latency dense GEMM family (BF16 + MXFP8)
shape: D3-32 r24: 96 requests / DP rank (384 verify rows R per TP4 group, n = 96 SP shard rows per GPU), L=135K, k=3
basis: baseline 8.9: gap512 EP16 in-step BF16 family (mxfp4 tree). current 6.7: PROJECTED nvfp4 r24 from the D-GEMM bench1 standalone per-call times (1 GPU, chained cold weights) with the best existing kernel per op x op count (+ separate MXFP8 input quant 1.5-3 us/call); no in-step nvfp4 step exists yet. achievable 2.80: perf model nvfp4_modelopt D3-32 r24 for my ops (model_gemm.py).
gap_analysis: bench1 (VR200, D3-32 per-GPU shapes, r24 = R384 gathered / n96 shard rows), best existing kernel vs model ach per call: kda_in MXFP8 14.6 (cuBLASLt) +3.0 quant vs 7.40 us; KDA o_proj MXFP8 6.3 +1.9 quant vs 2.07; shared gate_up MXFP8 12.2 +1.7 quant vs 6.80; shared down MXFP8 7.75 vs 3.45; latent down BF16 9.5 vs 3.84; latent up 7.5 vs 3.84; router 4.95 vs 1.05; DSA in 14.4 vs 8.06; q_b+wq_b 9.6 vs 2.81; DSA o_proj 9.2 vs 4.63; f_b 1.7 vs 0.23. Achieved weight streaming: 3-7.5 TB/s on 13-90 MB weights (only kda_in BF16 at R16 reaches 11.8 TB/s). Small weights (o_proj 22 MB MXFP8, router 13 MB, q_b/wq_b 13-14 MB) sit at a ~4-5 us per-kernel floor: launch + ramp + drain dominate. FlashInfer CUTLASS MXFP8 is 2-6x slower than CuTe DSL / cuBLASLt at every shape; trtllm-gen MXFP8 only competitive at <=16 rows. The existing Rubin TMEM-staged split-K (SplitKTmemGemm64) does not help at these shapes (latent down n96 8.5 us, shared down 15.6 us). Root cause in the vendored split-K (code-read, to confirm with ncu): its FP32 reduce mailbox ((split-1) x 128 x N-tile) is allocated beside the operand ring, so at 32-128 token columns any split > 2 leaves 1-2 ring stages -> too few weight bytes in flight; and rank 0 alone sums all partials.
inefficiencies: Weight streams at 3-7.5 TB/s vs 13.9 (16.5 die-local): too few bytes in flight per SM (vendored split-K: mailbox smem eats the ring above split 2; cuBLAS tile choice) [bench1 measured; per-kernel ncu pending]

Swap-AB split-K with one 128-row weight tile per CTA re-streams the activation tile per CTA: x bytes ~ T/128 of the weight bytes (0.75x at n96) [g_full sweep: time grows with token tile T at fixed weight]
Cluster split 7-8 over 28-56 weight tiles exceeds the co-scheduled cluster count -> 2 waves (split 6 is the ceiling for 28 tiles) [g_full + providers.py WIDE_B64 notes]
Per-kernel floor ~4-5 us on 13-22 MB weights (o_proj MXFP8, router, q_b, wq_b): launch/ramp/drain not hidden [bench1]
MXFP8 activation quant as separate kernels: 1.5-3.0 us x ~230 calls/step (~0.5 ms) [bench1 q_k3/q_fi]
Separate RS after o_proj partial GEMM (SpOproj gemm/mxfp8 tactic) [code]
FlashInfer CUTLASS MXFP8 backend 2-6x slower than CuTe DSL/cuBLASLt at decode shapes (avoid) [bench1]
sdec SP path refused MXFP8 linears (B4) -> FIXED on branch (Mxfp8Projection), unit tests pass
